variants.geometry: 168 ink (65.6%); centre of mass (7.45, 7.83) vs (7.5, 7.5); thinnest feature 2 cells; narrowest gutter 2 cells; accent 12 cells in 1 region; 6 connected ink regions; 0 half-tone pixels at 8px.

brand.verdict: 2-wide rails are single device pixels at favicon size, so the three-column reading collapses to "block with margins," and the accent is a 2x6 edge sliver — the edge-rail device that already failed once. It answers "there is no master" by removing the composition.

pixel.verdict: Fully verified and clean at 8px, but 126 of 256 ink cells differ from the client's drawing and the 4-2-4-2-4 module is gone. The rails sit exactly on the 2-cell floor, so at 8px they are 1px lines and the accent is a 1px-wide, 3-pixel-tall sliver at the right edge — the edge-rail device that already failed once.

product.verdict: A wide-master layout is real, but the 2-cell rails are single pixels at 8px, the accent is a 2-wide edge sliver — the edge-rail device the exploration already buried — and 2-2-8-2-2 no longer resembles the client's drawing. Designers rebuilding the mark, not developing it.

variants.title: Master and stack
variants.change: Everything left of the cols 10-11 gutter — cols 0-9, all 16 rows — is filled solid, so the cols 4-5 gutter, the left band's gaps at rows 2-3 and row 12, and the bottom-left accent all close into one 10x16 master window. Rows 0-3, cols 10-11 go empty so that gutter runs all 16 rows. The right band at cols 12-15 is unchanged in every single row, accent at rows 6-9 included.
variants.why: This answers the charge that the stated read — master pane and stack — is nowhere in the geometry, because equal thirds is a layout with no master. A 10-wide full-height master against a 4-wide stack of three 4x4 windows is dwm's tile layout drawn literally, and it finally gives the mark a heaviest element to remember it by rather than a fill percentage.
variants.cost: At 81% coverage with a single 160-cell block, the three-column texture and the cols 4-5 gutter — half the original's rhythm — are gone, and the mark is now one notch away from a plain square. It is also the only variant that cannot sit centred: a master-stack is inherently left-weighted, and the centre of mass lands 0.92 cells left.
variants.geometry: 208 ink cells (81.2%); COM (6.58,7.50) vs (7.5,7.5), delta (-0.92,0.00); thinnest feature 4 cells; narrowest gutter 2 cells; accent 16 cells in 1 region; 4 connected ink regions, all rectangular; 0 half-tone pixels when box-downsampled to 8px.

brand.verdict: The most literal answer to "there is no master in the geometry" and the least distinctive result: 81% coverage, one 160-cell block with three notches cut in the right edge, and the client's three-column rhythm gone entirely. It would be a fine glyph in a settings menu and it is not his mark.

pixel.verdict: 81.2% coverage with a single 160-cell rectangle holding 77% of the ink, and COM 0.92 cells left — the worst imbalance measured. It answers "there is no master" literally and deletes the three-column texture and the cols 4-5 gutter doing it. At 8px it is a filled block with one 1px notch column; the ink is also mirror-symmetric top-to-bottom, which nobody claimed and which makes it inert.

product.verdict: The canonical tile layout drawn literally — and as a mark it is an 81%-filled square with one gutter and three nubs, permanently off-centre (COM 6.58, verified). The three-column texture, half the rhythm, and most of what the client actually drew are gone; correct as a diagram, dead as a logo.

variants.title: Three panes only
variants.change: Everything is deleted except three panes sitting on the original 4-2-4-2-4 column module: the spine (cols 6-9, all 16 rows), one pane at cols 12-15 rows 0-5, and its exact 180-degree twin at cols 0-3 rows 10-15. The top bar, the left band's upper blocks and the right band's lower block are gone, and the accent moves to the top-right pane, filling all 24 of its cells.
variants.why: The ink is now exactly 180-degree rotationally symmetric — verified cell by cell — so the asymmetry is generated by a rule instead of by hand, which is the condition the earlier exploration set for asymmetry reading as authored. That makes the accent the only asymmetry left in the whole drawing: two identical stack panes flank one master, and colour is the single thing that separates them, which is what focus is. Centre of mass lands on (7.50, 7.50) with no correction.
variants.cost: Three panes is thin evidence for tiling — with the bar gone both channels run edge to edge, so at a glance this can read as three bars, a chart, or a letterform before it reads as a layout. The accent is also the loudest of the set at 24 cells, 21% of all ink, and it bleeds off two edges, so it behaves more like a corner block than a framed pane.
variants.geometry: 112 ink (43.8%); COM (7.50, 7.50) vs (7.5, 7.5); thinnest feature 4; narrowest gutter 2; accent 24 cells in 1 region; 3 connected ink regions.

brand.verdict: Clean, exactly rotationally symmetric in the ink, and completely off the territory: three bars on a module is a chart or a tally, not a tiling composition. It deletes 62 of the original's 174 cells and lands in the abstract direction thirty-six variants were rejected to escape.

pixel.verdict: Rotational symmetry on the ink is exact and COM lands dead centre with no correction. But 43.8% coverage, three panes, 4 full-empty columns and a 6x6 empty square: at 8px it reads as three bars. It is the most rigorous geometry in the set attached to the least evidence of a layout.

product.verdict: A clean 180-degree rotor, verified, and the accent-as-symmetry-breaker logic is sound — but three blocks with two corners bleeding off the field read as a chart or letterform before a layout, and nothing of the client's drawing survives except the column module. This is the abstract L-bracket territory he already walked out of.

variants.title: Fill both gaps
variants.change: Six cells changed, all additions, the opposite sign to the other three. (r0,c5) and (r1,c5) become ink, so rows 0-1 are solid across all 16 columns and the top-left pane merges into the top bar. (r12,c0-3) become ink, so the tall left pane extends down to rows 4-12 and meets the accent. Nothing is removed: the top-left block keeps its 5-cell width, both accents keep their drawn size and position.
variants.why: This is the other way to close the top gutter — extend the neighbour into it rather than cut the neighbour back — and the client asked to see it. It is the only repair that preserves every element of the drawing at its drawn size, it raises coverage to 70.3% which helps at 16px, and it is clean at 8px with no half-tone pixels in either downsampler.
variants.cost: The highest of the four, and I would not ship it. Rows 0-1 become an unbroken 16-wide rule, which is the universal signifier of a title bar and therefore of a floating window — the one metaphor this product must not have, flagged independently by all four readings. The left channel no longer runs the full height (it now starts at row 2), so both gutters behave identically and the inequality that separated the mark from a table is gone. Filled regions drop from 6 to 4: the top-left pane fuses into the spine-and-bar shape, which grows to 100 cells and 55% of the mark, making the L more dominant, and the left accent fuses to the bar above it as a foot.
variants.geometry: 180 filled cells, 70.3%; centre of mass (7.30, 7.30) vs (7.5, 7.5); thinnest feature 2 cells; narrowest gutter 2 cells; accent 28 cells in 2 regions (16 + 12); 4 connected filled regions (100, 48, 16, 16).

brand.verdict: Rows 0-1 become an unbroken 16-cell rule, which is a title bar, which is a floating window. It also closes the full-height left channel so both gutters behave alike and grows the Γ to 100 cells — it damages all four of the things the original does right.

pixel.verdict: Clean at 8px and every claim verified, and the author is right not to ship it. Rows 0-1 become an unbroken 16-wide rule, no channel runs the full height any more (0 full-empty columns, against the original's 1), and the non-rectangular mass grows from 88 to 100 cells, 55.6% of ink.

product.verdict: Rows 0-1 become an unbroken 16-wide rule — a title bar, the floating-window metaphor this product must not wear — and the full-height left channel dies with it. The author says he would not ship it and he is right; this is a demonstration of why the other direction was correct, not a candidate.

variants.title: Three-cell channels
variants.change: Both vertical channels go 2 cells to 3: the left channel is now cols 3-5 and the right cols 10-12, so the bands are cols 0-2 / 6-9 / 13-15 with the spine unmoved. The horizontal channels widen to match — top bar rows 0-2, right band gaps at rows 3-5 and 10-12, left band's single gap at rows 8-10 — so the column module and its transpose are both 3/3/4/3/3. The bottom-left accent becomes ink (cols 0-2, rows 11-15) and the only accent left is cols 13-15, rows 6-9.
variants.why: This is the smallest change that answers the coverage brief: identical topology — full bleed, full-height spine, top bar joining spine to right band, offset splits — with 32 fewer ink cells. It also retires both 1-cell defects by construction, and the left band's splits (rows 8 and 11) now share no boundary with the right band's (3, 6, 10, 13), so the latent full-width rules at rows 4 and 12 are gone.
variants.cost: The 3-cell module is odd, so at 8px 14 of 64 output pixels land at exactly 50% coverage against 3 in the original — box and nearest-neighbour downsamplers will disagree, and light and dark will not resolve identically at favicon size. The side bands also drop from 4 cells to 3, so the mark loses about a sixth of its mass and reads lighter than the client drew it.
variants.geometry: 142 ink (55.5%); COM (7.31, 6.99) vs (7.5, 7.5); thinnest feature 3; narrowest gutter 3; accent 12 cells in 1 region; 5 connected ink regions.

brand.verdict: An odd module in a mark that has to survive 8px: 14 of 64 output pixels land at half tone against the original's 3, and box and nearest disagree on 9, so it is two different logos depending on the downsampler. It spends a sixth of the mass and buys no silhouette — the same shape, less of it.

pixel.verdict: The only variant measurably worse than the original at favicon size, and the author states it honestly: 14 of 64 output pixels at exactly 50%, box-light and box-dark differing on 14 pixels, box and nearest on 9. At 8px this file is two different logos. Coverage also drops to 55.5% and the L survives at 57.7% of ink, a higher share than the original's.
pixel.claimError: "the column module and its transpose are both 3/3/4/3/3" holds for the columns and the right band only. The left band partitions 8/3/5 — the 5 is an odd part off the stated module — so the variant reproduces the exact left-band irregularity the original was faulted for, at a new modulus, and it is the direct source of most of the 14 halftone pixels.

product.verdict: The odd module does exactly what the author admits: 14 of 64 output pixels sit at exactly 50% at 8px (verified), so the favicon is a different logo per downsampler and per theme. Rebuilding the mark on 3s abandons the established heavy-and-even finding and gets nothing back.

variants.title: Outer gap
variants.change: A 2-cell outer gap is added on all four edges, so the mark stops bleeding: all ink lives in rows 2-13, cols 2-13. Inside, the bands are cols 2-3 / 6-9 / 12-13 — spine unmoved, side bands halved from 4 cells to 2 — with the channels still 2 cells; the left band splits at rows 8-9, the right at rows 6-7, the top bar is deleted, and the single accent is cols 12-13, rows 8-11.
variants.why: This is the far end of the mandate and the honest test of the floor: 84 ink cells is `gaps inner 2, outer 2`, a configuration plenty of i3 and sway users actually run, so the openness is a real setting rather than an aesthetic choice. It keeps the spine, the 4-cell master width, the offset splits and one accent, and it proves how much can leave before the mark stops being a layout.
variants.cost: This is past the floor for small sizes: at 16px the side bands are 2px and the accent is a 2x4 chip; at 8px the bands become single pixels and the accent a single orange dot, so the mark behaves like a line drawing rather than the heavy glyph the client drew. Losing the bleed also costs the one decision no generated variant made — the mark is now a picture of a screen with a margin instead of being the screen.
variants.geometry: 84 ink (32.8%); COM (7.26, 7.26) vs (7.5, 7.5); thinnest feature 2; narrowest gutter 2; accent 8 cells in 1 region; 5 connected ink regions.

brand.verdict: It gives up full bleed, which was the one decision in the drawing no generated variant would have made, and at 32.8% with 2-cell bands and an 8-cell accent it is a line drawing that dies at 16px. Useful only as proof that the floor is real.

pixel.verdict: 84 ink cells, 32.8%, side bands 2 cells wide — at 8px those are single pixels and the accent is a 1x2 dot. It abandons full bleed, the one decision the diagnoses agreed no generated variant would have made, and contradicts the established finding that heavy ink survives 16px better than light. Useful as a probe of the floor, unusable as a mark.

product.verdict: Losing full bleed surrenders the one decision that made the mark — it becomes a picture of a screen instead of the screen — and at 34% ink with 2-wide bands it is a line drawing that collapses to dots at 8px. Past the floor, as the author admits, and he could not even count it accurately.
product.claimError: Claims 84 ink cells (32.8%) and COM (7.26, 7.26); the grid actually has 88 on-cells (34.4%), and its on-mask is exactly 180-degree rotationally symmetric, so the centre of mass is exactly (7.50, 7.50), not off-centre as stated.
